scope: Proposition 5.3 (Transitivity for every parameter tree) of the manuscript “Witnessed symmetric choice is strictly stronger than choiceless polynomial time with counting” (preprints/Witnessed-symmetric-choice-is-strictly-stronger-than-choiceless-polynomial-time-with-counting-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 243 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 d648a0d83b5f41b1), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 20. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let Ab be a grid structure, α ∈ P, and x a compatible prefix of length j < r. For every ordered pair s, s′ ∈ D(α, x) there is g ∈ M(α, x) with g(s) = s′. The map g preserves the full input, fixes every block setwise, and fixes every atom of x individually. Consequently every selection path for α chooses one atom from each edge outside T, in order, maintains compatibility, and then stabilizes with the dummy choice. All its witnessing maps respect α and the entire preceding history.
